summary: Third Marengo tower, a 100-foot stair-type built 1987 in Ashland County; preceded by a 1939 tower destroyed in 1941; state network decommissioned 2015; listed as standing.

facts.design: 100-foot stair-type tower, likely an Aermotor MC-39 (present tower, erected 1987)

visit.trail_note: A visitor report on the NHLR page says the road is heavily rutted on a small stretch. No public access level is established in the sources read.

events.note: First 100-foot Wisconsin Standard tower on the point, per NHLR
Destroyed in a fall windstorm, September 1941, per NHLR
Replacement 65-foot steel tower with enclosed cab; NHLR says the mountain 'presumably' stood vacant until approximately 1949, when photographs show a replacement
Present 100-foot stair-type tower erected, likely an Aermotor MC-39; the 65-foot tower had served until the late 1980s
Saw active service until 2015, when Wisconsin decommissioned its lookout network; WJFW says the 72 towers still in use were decommissioned that year

notes_for_editor: The tower history rests almost entirely on one long NHLR narrative (with photographs credited to WI DNR and the USFS, not fetched). The Park Falls origin is a visitor comment and is uncorroborated; the register's own 'likely surplus' is a suggestion, and the story labels both. Date conflict to watch: the register puts the 1939 tower's destruction in September 1941, while a Chequamegon Bay history PDF (chequamegonbay-history.com, ChequamegonCJ134WindsAndFloods.pdf) describes a late August 1941 cloudburst and windstorm across the Ashland area. That PDF does not mention this tower, so the register's date stands, but it is unreconciled. The 'Staffed? No' line on the register is a visit-report field and is not quoted, because the page text splits it across lines. Access level is not established; the record's 'access: unknown' stands. Possible mention of a Marengo tower near Mellon in a Facebook group post was not used.
